core_obligations: Induct on n, using the exact sequence of the hyperplane section to obtain chi(P^n, F(d)) - chi(P^n, F(d-1)) = chi(H, G(d)) (proof lines 6779-6796).
Use that H is isomorphic to projective (n-1)-space, so that by the induction hypothesis the right-hand side is a polynomial in d (proof lines 6797-6798).

Conclude with the arithmetic fact that a function on the integers whose first difference is a polynomial is itself a polynomial, which the author states and attributes to the cited algebra lemma (proof lines 6799-6803).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an infinite base field via the induction-step lemma.
Compare consecutive Euler characteristics through the hyperplane restriction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the function d mapping to chi(P^n, F(d)) is a polynomial for a coherent sheaf on projective n-space. The proof inducts on n using the hyperplane section sequence: after enlarging the base field so that a suitable section exists, it obtains the identity chi(P^n, F(d)) - chi(P^n, F(d-1)) = chi(H, G(d)) and notes that H is projective (n-1)-space, so by induction the right-hand side is a polynomial (proof lines 6779-6798). The conclusion then uses that a function whose first difference is a polynomial is itself a polynomial; the author states that arithmetic fact without proof and points to the corresponding algebra lemma (proof lines 6799-6803). H2: the induction through the hyperplane sequence is the substance, and the omitted arithmetic fact is routine and explicitly identified.
